div.head: Becwæð 1
div.ab: . . . Hit becwæð ⁊ becwæl sé ðe hit ahte mid fullan folcrihte, swa swa hit his yldran mid feo ⁊ mid feore rihte begeatan ⁊ letan ⁊ læfdan ðam to gewealde, ðe hy wel uðan.
Hit becwæð ⁊ becwæl se ðe hit ahte mid fullan folcrihte, swa swa hit his yldran mid feo ⁊ mid feore rihte begeatan ⁊ letan ⁊ læfdan ðam to gewealde, ðe hy wel uðan.

...dies vermachte und verstarb der, welcher es nach vollem Landrecht besass, so wie es seine Voreltern, durch Geldzahlung und durch Naturalienabgabe[?], richtig erworben und denjenigen, welchen [oder dem, welchem] sie es frei [völlig] schenkten, zur Verfügung überlassen und hinterlassen hatten.

… this [land] was bequeathed by him who held it with full folk-right — and he died — just as his forebears had rightly acquired it with money and with payment in kind[?], and had left and bequeathed it into the power of those [or him] to whom they freely [fully] granted it.

That he bequeathed and [thereafter] died: he who owned it in full customary law, just as his ancestors lawfully acquired it with their property and person and left and made over to the keeping to whom they had good cause to grant it.

div.note: U: translator probably Wormald, The Making of English Law (named in the original spreadsheet’s sub-header rows): check; Liebermann prints H (Textus Roffensis f. 95, after a charm, c. 1120) and B (Cambridge, Corpus Christi College 383, p. 89, after a charm as in H, c. 1125). K is B; H is also given here. The beginning is lacking, perhaps ‘Swa ic hit hæbbe, swa’ as in 2. Leo set the text out rhythmically. ‘dies’ means the land now disputed against me, the holder, by you. ‘feore’: Liebermann would correct to ‘feorme’ (payment in kind; compare Genesis 2659 ‘mid feo and mid feorme’); the formula ‘æt feo oððe æt feore’ (EGu 12) misled the archetype. B's ‘his’ is corrected from ‘is’. Liebermann dates Becwæð c. 1020–c. 1060. The pairs ‘becwæð ⁊ becwæl’, ‘feo ⁊ feore’, ‘letan ⁊ læfdan’ alliterate.; F: corrected against Liebermann, Gesetze I (date in the running heads), October 2026 (was “c.1020–c.1060; c.990–c.1020 (Wormald)”, now “c.1020–c.1060 (Liebermann); c.990–c.1020 (Wormald)”); F: corrected against Liebermann, Gesetze I (date at the head of the text); Wormald, Making of English Law I; Whitelock, English Historical Documents I, October 2026 (was “c.1020–c.1060 (Liebermann); c.990–c.1020 (Wormald)”, now “c.1020–c.1060 (Liebermann, I p. 400); c.990–c.1020 (Wormald, MEL p. 385)”); BQ: page of each of Liebermann’s texts and of his German, checked against Liebermann, Gesetze I (our double-read transcription), October 2026 (e.g. was “(empty)”, now “H 400; B 400; German 400”; 5 rows of Becwæð)

Vgl. Gl Erbgang 7; Gastung 6. 18. Die Formel feoh ⁊ feorm s. II Cn 16¹. Laut Urkk. muss oft der Empfänger von Land ælce geare ane feorme leisten (Thorpe Dipl. 531. 554); ein Wald wird verkauft gegen 40 peniga ⁊ 8 ambra cornes (Ke 1315). Unmöglich ist der bisherige Text feore. Wörtlich ergäbe er Unsinn: mit Leben Bezahltes kann man nicht vermachen. Übertragener Sinn ‘Einsetzung der Persönlichkeit, etwa im Kriegsdienst’ oder ‘[gute] Lebensführung’ ist nicht bezeugt. Ebensowenig kann das Grundstück ‘samt Fahrhabe und Lebendigem’ gemeint sein; letzteres wird durch ‘Leute, Lebendes (men, libbend, cwic)’ ausgedrückt, nie durch ‘Leben’.—Vgl. mid rihte begeat Swer 3, 1

Cf. Gl Erbgang 7; Gastung 6. 18. For the formula feoh ⁊ feorm, see II Cn 16¹. According to charters the recipient of land must often render ælce geare ane feorme (Thorpe Dipl. 531. 554); a wood is sold for 40 peniga ⁊ 8 ambra cornes (Ke 1315). The previous reading feore is impossible. Taken literally it would give nonsense: what has been paid for with life cannot be bequeathed. A figurative sense ‘staking of one’s person, say in military service’ or ‘[good] conduct of life’ is not attested. Nor can the property ‘together with chattels and living stock’ be meant; the latter is expressed by ‘people, living things (men, libbend, cwic)’, never by ‘life’. — Cf. mid rihte begeat Swer 3, 1
‘wohl gönnten’ Schmid; ‘gifted’ Thorpe. Allein es ist Urkundenausdruck für bene tradere, concedere, donare; z. B. he þa boc unnendre handa hire to let; a. 961 Bi 1064
